method: CAD pieces: ah001_cad_meshes split meshes (build_ah001.py localize_mesh), vertices already in robot body frames; body frames ISB (x anterior, y superior, z right) at the pelvis datum (AGENTS.md 2026-10-27 ruling; build_ah001.py cad_to_isb normalizes through the pelvis part 02_01_PE_ datum)
robot joint anchors = CAD anchors (build_ah001.py uses the audit joint anchor_a; MuJoCo body offsets = the anchor deltas)
OpenSim neutral transforms parsed from gait2392_robotbody.osim and validated EXACTLY (max|dT| < 1e-9) against geometry_20261103/extraction_robotbody.json bodyTransformsInGround.neutral
registration anchor: align the HIP centers (translate(hipOS - hipR)); pelvis frames both ISB so rotations are identity; knee/ankle mismatches are then measured, not absorbed

robot knee state vs OpenSim knee_angle_r: four-bar solved for (theta_back, theta_front) at each sampled theta_shank; flexion mapping theta_shank(kappa) = sFlex*(kappa*-1 - flex0) verified by reconstructing the femur/shank axis angle

registration_errors_mm.hip_definition: robot hip ball (MuJoCo thigh_r offset = CAD knob-pin anchor) vs OpenSim hip_r pelvis_offset
registration_errors_mm.knee_definition: robot KB pin (four-bar knee-bottom pivot = shank_r origin) carried on the hip-aligned femur segment vs OpenSim knee center of record = the TIBIA BODY ORIGIN at neutral (gait2392 knee: rotation axis at the femur origin, knee-angle splines carry the tibia; both knee_r offsets are 0); residual AFTER hip alignment. Dominated by the SEGMENT SPLIT difference: the AH001 femur link (hip->KB pin) is longer and its shank (KB->foot) shorter than the OpenSim femur/tibia split; per-segment anchoring keeps each SDF piece correct while this number is the honest cross-model error

knee_station_residual_over_sweep_mm.note: pose-dependent residual: robot four-bar KB pin vs OpenSim moving-pivot tibia origin, same kappa; the two knee KINEMATICS differ (splines vs four-bar) -- inherent to CAD mechanism + OpenSim routing, quoted not hidden

registration_errors_mm.ankle_definition: robot foot_r origin = mesh-derived distal tibia end center (foot_geometry.py distal_center), welded-foot station vs OpenSim ankle_r location; the robot has NO ankle pin in this build (welded foot), so this is a station error, not a joint error

four_bar.flexion_axis_note: mesh-PCA long axes (CORRECTED_SCENE method) of record; the pin-based alternative differs by the anterior four-bar mount offset (~10 deg)

uncertainty_rule: Attachment searches may use this model for clearance, but a large attachment excursion justified by uncertain registration is FORBIDDEN: the campaign patch bounds stay anatomically tight (surface patch radius + mount standoff in mm, fr_patch/fr_setup conventions).
limitations: cloud-only bodies (Spine, Pelvis_R, Sacrum, Talus, Calcaneus, Toes): sparse-sample distance, conservative; NN bounds recorded per cloud
robot hip is a BALL joint mapped by the OpenSim hip axes sequence (exact for the OpenSim joint model; the physical robot hip has the same axes at its zero pose, both ISB)
the SDF sign uses the closest-triangle normal with a ray-parity consistency check on the near-surface shell (agreement recorded per body)
pelvis/foot grids at 3 mm voxels, others 2.5 mm; SDF clamped at +/-30 mm; queries outside the grid return +clamp (conservative for clearance)
